chapters.title: How a scene gets filmed
chapters.say: How does a web page become a video? One frame at a time.

beats.say: This loop is the heart of the renderer. It runs once for every frame of the scene.
First, it asks the page to draw itself at one exact moment, and the page answers a single question: did anything change?
beats.note: draw the frame at time t

beats.say: Only when the picture changed does it take a new screenshot.
Either way, a frame goes down the pipe to the encoder. A still moment just sends the same picture again.
When the encoder exits cleanly, the temporary file gets its real name, so a half finished render can never pass for a complete one.

nodes.label: Storyboard
nodes.desc: Chapters, sentences, and what to show

nodes.label: Voice
nodes.desc: One clip per sentence, made locally

nodes.label: Timeline
nodes.desc: Each beat lasts as long as its sentence

beats.say: Zooming out, filming is one of five steps. It starts with a storyboard: the chapters, the sentences, and what to show for each.
Every sentence is spoken by a voice model that runs locally. No account or key is needed.
The length of each spoken clip sets the timeline, so the picture always follows the voice.
Then each scene is filmed, the way you just saw.
Finally, narration and sound effects are mixed in, and the chapters are joined.
That is the whole pipeline. Don't read. Just watch.
